title: Two-Player Map · Pair relay
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Two-Player Map · Pair relay with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Choose two players and three familiar landmarks in an imagined room. One player places the first landmark on paper; the other adds the remaining two after a spoken description. The finished map matches the agreed relative positions. Form pairs. On each pair’s turn, both people make separate attempts with fresh challenges, helping only their partner. The pair earns one point only if both succeed. Each pair has two turns. Highest score wins.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4, 6 or 8 players; materials: Paper and pencil.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Two-Player Map, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The finished map matches the agreed relative positions.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
recall.why: The finished map matches the agreed relative positions.
